Thought: To solve this problem, I need to recall the electronic configuration of sodium (Na) and then determine what happens when it becomes a Na+ ion.

Sodium (Na) has an atomic number of 11, which means it has 11 electrons in its neutral state. The electronic configuration of neutral sodium is 1s²2s²2p⁶3s¹.

When sodium loses an electron to form Na+, it loses the electron from its outermost shell, which is the 3s¹ electron. This means Na+ has 10 electrons, and its electronic configuration becomes 1s²2s²2p⁶.

Looking at the options:
A. 1s²2s²2p⁶ - This matches the configuration I determined for Na+
B. 1s²2s²2p⁶3s¹ - This is the configuration of neutral Na, not Na+
C. 1s²2s²2p⁶3s² - This has too many electrons for Na+
D. 1s²2s²2p⁸ - This is not a valid configuration as the 2p orbital can only hold a maximum of 6 electrons
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
